root_cause.text: The arm64 ioremap_prot() function was directly using the user-space pgprot_t value (which includes user permission bits like PTE_USER) to create kernel mappings, causing kernel access to fail on PAN-enabled systems when the resulting mapping retained user-only permission controls.
root_cause.evidence: The patch extracts only the memory type attribute bits (PTE_ATTRINDX_MASK) from the user pgprot_t and applies them to PAGE_KERNEL, while explicitly asserting that the input is a user mapping via `WARN_ON_ONCE(!(user_prot_val & PTE_USER))`. The original code at line 269 simply aliased `ioremap_prot` directly to `__ioremap_prot`, passing through all pgprot_t bits including permission controls that are incompatible with kernel access on systems with Privileged Access Never (PAN) enabled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation and controlled merging of user-supplied protection flags in ioremap_prot to prevent privilege escalation through incorrect memory attribute configuration.
intent_record.what: Replaced a simple macro definition `#define ioremap_prot __ioremap_prot` with a static inline function that validates the user_prot parameter contains the PTE_USER bit, modifies the protection flags using __pgprot_modify to preserve only the attribute index bits, and calls __ioremap_prot with the computed protection. Also replaced `#define _PAGE_IOREMAP PROT_DEVICE_nGnRE` with an inline `#define ioremap(addr, size)` macro that explicitly calls __ioremap_prot with PROT_DEVICE_nGnRE.
intent_record.how: The change adds runtime validation that user-provided protection flags include the PTE_USER bit, returning NULL if validation fails. It also enforces that only the attribute index portion of user-provided flags is used, with the rest of the protection attributes coming from PAGE_KERNEL. This prevents privilege escalation or incorrect memory attribute mapping by ensuring user-supplied protection values cannot override critical kernel protection settings. The ioremap macro now explicitly specifies PROT_DEVICE_nGnRE instead of relying on an indirect constant definition.
